chief_complaint: feeling of bulge in vagina and pelvic heaviness
hpi_details: A 65-year-old woman presents with a vaginal bulge sensation and pelvic heaviness that have gradually worsened.
ideas: thinks she may have pelvic organ prolapse
concerns: She is worried that the lump is a malignant tumor or that she will require major surgery with a long, painful recovery.
expectations: She hopes to find out what is causing the bulge and whether it can be managed with pelvic floor exercises or a support ring rather than an operation.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Cystocele / anterior vaginal wall prolapse evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Cystocele / anterior vaginal wall prolapse is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Cystocele vaginal prolapse: Pelvic floor exercises, pessary fitting, or surgical repair, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.

history.answer: I feel like something is bulging or falling out of my vagina, and there is a constant heavy dragging sensation down there.
I first noticed a mild fullness about six months ago, but the bulge has become much more noticeable and bothersome over the past two months.
The bulge is right at the opening of my vagina, and the heaviness stays deep in my lower pelvic area without spreading anywhere else.
It feels like a smooth, soft ball pressing downward, accompanied by an uncomfortable dragging pressure that gets worse as the day goes on.
In the morning when I wake up it barely bothers me, but after I stand or walk for a few hours it drops down lower and feels much heavier.
Standing for a long time, walking, coughing, or carrying heavy groceries makes it bulge out more. Lying down flat gives me immediate relief.
I feel like I cannot fully empty my bladder, and sometimes a few drops of urine leak out when I cough or sneeze.
Sometimes when I finish urinating, I have to push the bulge back inside with my fingers to let the rest of the urine flow out.
No, I have never had a complete blockage where I could not pee at all, and there is no pain or burning when I pass urine.
My bowels are regular, and I do not have constipation or need to push against the vagina to have a bowel movement.
No, I haven't noticed any bleeding, spotting, or unusual discharge from my vagina.
The skin feels slightly irritated from rubbing against my underwear when I walk, but I haven't noticed any open sores or raw spots.
I have not had any fever, chills, or unexplained weight loss.
I have never experienced a prolapse or bulge like this before, and I haven't been evaluated for it until today.
I tried lying down more often to rest and wearing firmer underwear, which helps temporarily, but the bulge comes right back when I stand up.
I watch my young grandson twice a week and lift him frequently, but I do not have a chronic cough.
I delivered three children through normal vaginal births in my twenties and thirties, and two of them weighed over four kilograms at birth.
It makes it uncomfortable to take my usual daily walks or do housework, and I find myself having to sit down to rest frequently.
A close friend of mine had her bladder drop years ago, so I am wondering if I might have pelvic organ prolapse or a fallen bladder.
I'm terrified that this bulge might be a cancerous growth, or that I'll need major surgery that leaves me bedridden.
I was hoping you could check what this lump actually is and let me know if there's a simple support ring or exercise to fix it without surgery.
I have mild high blood pressure, but no diabetes, heart disease, or other medical conditions.
I had my appendix removed when I was twenty-two, but I have never had any pelvic or gynecologic surgery.
I take amlodipine 5 milligrams once every morning for my blood pressure, along with a daily multivitamin.
I have no known allergies to any medications.
I went through natural menopause around age fifty-one and have never taken hormone replacement therapy.
My husband and I are still somewhat intimate, but intercourse has felt awkward and uncomfortable with the bulge, so we have put that on hold lately.
I have never smoked cigarettes in my life.
I only have an occasional glass of wine on special occasions, perhaps once or twice a month.
I am retired from clerical work and live in an apartment with my husband.
My mother also suffered from pelvic heaviness and bladder dropping in her seventies, but there is no family history of cancer.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/78 mmHg, heart rate 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.6 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, comfortable-appearing elderly female in no acute distress.
Soft and non-tender throughout; no palpable abdominal or pelvic masses, and the bladder is not distended.
External genitalia show normal postmenopausal changes with a smooth anterior vaginal bulge visible at the introitus on straining.
Bivalve speculum examination confirms marked anterior vaginal wall descent consistent with cystocele; the cervix and posterior wall are well supported, and there are no mucosal ulcerations.
Normal sphincter tone with no rectal masses, tenderness, or significant posterior wall defect.
No inguinal or femoral hernia identified on either side.
